Similarly §7.7's `News.text` validation — "must contain a proper noun/number/date" — and §2's claim that the every-sentence rule is "a hard rule and a grep-able one" are not implementable for proper nouns.
issues.fix: Put the single list in `config/banned-words.json`, reference it from both sections, drop "holistic" or list the specific collocations, and restate the proper-noun rule honestly: the CI check greps for a digit or a capitalised word that is not sentence-initial and **warns**; it is a review prompt in the §11 rubric, not a build failure.

issues.problem: Three of the fourteen questions are not open. Q1 ("Is satishregonda.in actually registered, and where?") is answerable in one RDAP/whois lookup — the three agents ran DoH A/NS queries, which cannot distinguish unregistered from registered-and-undelegated, and the answer determines whether Phase 0 is a nameserver change or a purchase. Q12 (RAFT expansion) restates a decision §5 already made with three grounds — it is a notification, not a question. Q6 is half-answered (nine CC-BY, four bronze already established) but asks as if from zero.
issues.fix: Run RDAP on satishregonda.in and raftwaters.in before the call and replace Q1 with the finding plus the one thing only he has (registrar credentials). Move Q12 out of Open Questions into a "Decisions we made for you — say no if you disagree" list alongside the Play Store "Suresh Regonda" typo. Narrow Q6 to the 26 papers whose status is genuinely unknown, and attach the list.

issues.problem: Phase 0's checklist requires "two named account owners" on Cloudflare and GitHub, but the person is only identified in Open Q14 — the last question in the document, tagged as a launch concern. Phase 0 cannot complete as written. Separately the phase efforts sum to 14.5 days (0.5+2+3+3+4+2) against a stated "~17 working days", with no line for content sign-off with him (§2 carries a `[PLACEHOLDER]` requiring his approval of the bio), no revision round, and no allocation for the three seeded blog posts Open Q11 promises.
issues.fix: Move the second-owner question into the Phase 0 "From him" list. Restate the total as 14.5 days of build + 2.5 days of review/revision/seed-writing = 17, with the review days named: bio and theme-prose sign-off (1), the 39-citation proofread with him (0.5), three seeded posts (1).

issues.problem: The site publishes named students with photographs and email addresses, and the brief has no consent, removal or obfuscation policy — while it does carefully flag the two unlicensed press photographs. It also rejects a contact form partly because "his address is already public on the IITH directory", which is not true of every student's address, and cites DPDP notice obligations three times as a reason to reject tools while shipping no privacy notice.
issues.fix: Add to §7.6: a `consent` checkbox required before a photo renders, and a one-line removal process in the RUNBOOK (clear the row's `photo` and `email`, press Publish now — alumni keep their thesis line). Publish student contact as a Scholar/website link by default and email only where `email_public` is ticked. Add a 120-word `/colophon/#privacy` block: no cookies, no analytics beacon, no forms, no personal data collected — which is true under the fixes above and discharges the DPDP notice in one paragraph.

issues.problem: The failure table is the strongest section in the brief but is missing the four most likely editor errors: a Doc referenced by `body_doc_url` is deleted, moved or un-shared (drive.files.export 404); two rows share an `id`/`slug` (uniqueness is asserted but Sheets cannot enforce it and no formula is specified, unlike `people_ids`); a `Published/` blog Doc has no settings table or a malformed one; and a `Publications.theme` value that no longer matches any `Research.slug` after a theme is removed.
issues.fix: Add four rows with the same shape as the existing ones — what he sees, and the fix. Add a duplicate-detector formula on every `id`/`slug` column (`=IF(COUNTIF(A:A,A3)>1,"❌ duplicate","")`) so it fails in the sheet, not at build, consistent with the brief's own stated preference for client-side validation.

issues.section: CUT — §8.1 Search, Fallback CMS, OG images
issues.problem: Three infrastructure choices add dependency, budget and handover surface without serving a named audience need. **Pagefind**: 39 publications already have filter chips and a 25-line filter; nobody search-boxes a personal academic site, and it has no route, no UI and no budget line. **Sveltia CMS at /admin**: a second, unfamiliar editing surface for a professor who will never open it, requiring him to hold a GitHub PAT — while `pnpm run eject` plus the committed Markdown already delivers the longevity guarantee it is justified by. **Satori/resvg OG generation**: a whole render step plus an unsubsetted OTF kept in the repo, for a site whose sharing surface is a Scholar profile and a WhatsApp forward.
issues.fix: Cut all three. Keep the filter chips as real URLs (`/publications/?theme=…` server-rendered, so Scholar's no-JS-navigation rule still holds). Replace Sveltia with one RUNBOOK page: "if Google is gone, run `pnpm run eject` and edit Markdown in GitHub's web editor" — the same capability, zero config, zero PAT. Replace generated OG cards with three static 1200×630 images (site, research, writing) referenced by route type. Saves roughly a day of Phase 3/4 and about 60 KB of JS budget.

issues.section: CUT — §5 /research/krishna-serayu-climate-extremes/, §7.7 Manual tab, §6.4 per-paper figure, §7.6 current_position, §7.1 scholar_citations
issues.problem: Five items add content-model surface, maintenance burden or rights exposure without a reader who needs them. The krishna-serayu **theme page** is a completed 2020 project given a full page, a body Doc, a required figure and a slug — and no entry point in the IA. The **Manual tab** duplicates Talks/Tools/Publications with four more categories, none of which render anywhere. The **per-paper figure** has no model field and would mean reproducing publisher figures 39 times. **`current_position` alongside `first_position`** is exactly the two-sources-that-drift problem the brief argues against for CVs, and it obliges him to re-survey alumni forever. **`scholar_citations`/`_h`/`_i10`** are defined in §7.1 while §12 Q13 recommends against ever showing them.
issues.fix: Cut all five. Krishna-Serayu becomes a row in the /research/ past-projects table with the workshop report PDF linked and the FGD date named — the archival value is preserved, the orphan disappears, and the redirect points there. Delete the Manual tab. Delete the paper-page figure block. Keep `first_position` only (with `first_position_year`). Delete the three Scholar-metric fields and keep the quiet Scholar link the brief already recommends.

issues.section: CUT — §4.4 item 2 masthead band, §12 Q10 Telugu page, §4.1
issues.problem: Three smaller items. The **8%-opacity full-bleed hydrograph band behind the home masthead** is decoration sitting directly behind the LCP element and is the one place the brief bends its own rule against full-width decorative backgrounds — while the divider and footer glyph carry the same idea at no cost. The **Telugu page** has no answer in the type system: the font subset is Latin-only, so a `lang="te"` page would ship with a system fallback that contradicts §4.1 and rubric item 5. The §4.1 **font binary diff, the fontTools build command, and the x-height arithmetic** are excellent justification but are three pages of appendix inside a client-facing brief.
issues.fix: Keep the section divider and footer glyph; drop the masthead band. Move the Telugu page to a costed option: it needs a fourth family (Noto Serif Telugu, +~80 KB), a translator, and a maintenance commitment — and it is out unless he commits to all three. Move the font diff, build command and x-height table to `docs/typography.md` and leave a three-line summary in §4.1.

An Education/Appointments collection and a Service collection: the home trajectory strip, /about/'s education, appointments and service blocks, and the generated CV all render records that no tab holds
